description: Verify that DUT drops a gratuitous ARP Response carrying an unknown proto_type and re-resolves on next egress — proto_type variant of ARP_22
approach:
[Objective]
Same two-phase pattern as ARP_22; here the bad announcement carries an unknown proto_type instead of an unknown hw_type. The receiver must reject before learning — confirmed by observing DUT's own ARP Request on the subsequent UDP egress.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: gratuitous ARP Response injected
   • opcode      = 2
   • proto_type  = some unknown value   ← bad
   • sender_ip   = HOST-1-IP / sender_mac = MAC-ADDR1 / target_ip = HOST-1-IP

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup
   ⇒ stimulates DUT to send a UDP response to HOST-1-IP.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → broadcast: ARP Request for HOST-1-IP
   • DUT's UDP must not use MAC-ADDR1 as eth_dst

[Pass condition]
DUT emits its own ARP Request for HOST-1-IP and does not use MAC-ADDR1.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_udp_used_injected_mac — UDP eth_dst was MAC-ADDR1 → malformed announcement learned
• Fail_no_dut_arp_request — no DUT ARP Request → reception path incomplete

verdicts.Pass: DUT dropped the malformed gratuitous and resolved via its own Request — normal
verdicts.Fail_udp_used_injected_mac: DUT used MAC-ADDR1 in UDP — silently learned a malformed announcement
verdicts.Fail_no_dut_arp_request: DUT did not resolve via its own Request — reception path incomplete
